title: Work & colleagues
goal: Chat with colleagues, follow meetings and deadlines, write a polite message to your boss, ask for leave and get through a job interview in Sindhi.
intro:
Office Sindhi is a mix: the grammar is Sindhi, but half the nouns are English — **ميٽنگ**, **ڊيڊلائن**, **رپورٽ**, **اي ميل** — and with your boss everything shifts up a gear into the formal register: **سائين**, **ميڊم**, **جي، حاضر**, **عرض آهي ته …**.

In this unit you'll learn that formal register properly, and the **passive** that fills office notices, emails and the news: **فيصلو ڪيو ويو** 'it was decided', **ميٽنگ ملتوي ڪئي وئي** 'the meeting was postponed'. You'll also learn to ask for a day off, push a deadline and talk about yourself in an interview.

grammar.title: The formal register: talking to your boss and writing to the office
grammar.body:
In unit 18 you met the levels of politeness. At work you need the whole formal kit, and you need to know when to switch.

**You.** Always **توهان** to a boss, a client or anyone senior — never تون. For very senior people you'll also hear **پاڻ** and **جناب**. The verb is **plural even for one person**, and so is talk *about* them: **علي صاحب ميٽنگ ۾ آهن** 'Mr Ali is in a meeting', **سائين آيا آهن** 'Sir has arrived'.

**Address.** **سائين** to a man (also the respectful word for 'he' when talking about the boss), **ميڊم** to a woman, or the name + **صاحب** (شاهه صاحب، علي صاحب). For a woman, name + **صاحبه** or ميڊم.

**Answers.** **جي سائين / جي ميڊم** 'yes sir / ma'am', **حاضر** 'right away, at your service', **جي ها** 'yes indeed'. A bare ها sounds offhand.

**Requests.** The -و and -جو forms, **مهرباني ڪري**, and the question **ڇا … سگهو ٿا؟** 'could you …?'. In writing: **عرض آهي ته …** or **گذارش آهي ته …** 'I respectfully request that …', followed by a subjunctive or a passive: موڪل ڏني وڃي 'that leave be given'.

**Formal words.** Formal Sindhi swaps in Persian and Arabic words: **تشريف رکو** 'please be seated' (for ويهو), **مڪمل** 'complete' (for پورو), **گڏجاڻي** 'meeting' (for ميٽنگ).

**A message to the boss:** **محترم سائين،** … **عرض آهي ته** … **مهرباني.** **توهان جو** (man) / **توهان جي** (woman), + name.

**When to switch down:** colleagues your own age become **تون** and **يار** within days — in the corridor, at lunch, on WhatsApp. Switch back up in meetings, in front of the boss and in email.

examples.en: Yes ma'am, the report is ready.

grammar.title: The passive: ڪيو ويو 'it was done', چئجي ٿو 'it is said'
grammar.body:
Office notices, emails and the news are full of sentences where the doer is left out: *it was decided*, *the meeting has been postponed*. Sindhi has two ways to do this.

**1. Past participle + وڃڻ**
Take the past participle of the verb (ڪيو، ڏنو، موڪليو …) and add **وڃڻ** 'go' in any tense. Both parts agree with the **thing** that the action happens to:

فيصلو **ڪيو ويو** — it was decided (فيصلو m)
ميٽنگ ملتوي **ڪئي وئي** — the meeting was postponed (ميٽنگ f)
رپورٽون **موڪليون ويون** — the reports were sent (f pl)

Other tenses: **ڪيو وڃي ٿو** 'is done' (regularly) · **ڪيو ويندو** 'will be done' · **ڪيو ويو آهي** 'has been done' · and the subjunctive **ڪيو وڃي** 'that it be done' (after عرض آهي ته, گذارش آهي ته).

The person it's done *to* takes **کي**: **مون کي ٻڌايو ويو** ته … 'I was told that …'.

**2. The short -ij- passive**
Sindhi also has an old, very compact passive made by adding **-ij-** to the stem: **ڪجي ٿو** 'it is done, one does', **چئجي ٿو** 'it is said', **ٻڌجي ٿو** 'it is heard' = 'rumour has it', **پيئجي** 'is drunk' (هتي سگريٽ نه پيئجي 'no smoking here'). Use it for customs, rules and gossip — recognise it first, then try it.

**The trap:** don't confuse the passive **ٿي ويو** with **ڪيو ويو**. ڪم پورو **ٿي** ويو = 'the work got finished' (it just happened); ڪم پورو **ڪيو** ويو = 'the work was completed' (by someone, deliberately).

dialogue.title: Monday at the office
dialogue.setting: Monday morning at a software company on Shahrah-e-Faisal, Karachi. Marvi catches her colleague Asad at the coffee machine; later Asad goes in to see their boss, Shah sahib.

lines.en: What time? Nobody's even told me.

lines.speaker: Marvi

lines.en: At eleven. And listen — the deadline has been extended to Friday.

lines.speaker: Asad
lines.native: شڪر! پر جمعي تي منهنجي ڀيڻ جي شادي آهي. موڪل وٺڻي پوندي.
lines.roman: shukur! para jumʿe te munhinjī bheṇa jī shādī āhe. mokala vaṭhaṇī pavandī.
lines.en: Thank God! But my sister's wedding is on Friday. I'll have to take the day off.

lines.speaker: Marvi

lines.roman: ta poi aʄu ī darxāsta ɗe. shāh sāhib subuh jo suṭhe moḍa meṃ hundā āhin.
lines.en: Then ask today. Shah sahib's always in a good mood in the morning.

lines.speaker: Shah sahib
lines.native: اچو اسد، تشريف رکو. خير آهي؟
lines.roman: acho asad, tashrīfa rakho. xairu āhe?
lines.en: Come in, Asad, have a seat. All well?

lines.speaker: Asad
lines.native: سائين، عرض آهي ته جمعي تي منهنجي ڀيڻ جي شادي آهي. ڇا مون کي موڪل ملي سگهي ٿي؟
lines.roman: sāīṃ, ʿarzu āhe ta jumʿe te munhinjī bheṇa jī shādī āhe. chhā moṃ khe mokala milī saghe thī?
lines.en: Sir, if I may — my sister's wedding is on Friday. Could I have the day off?

lines.speaker: Shah sahib
lines.native: مبارڪون! پر رپورٽ جو ڇا ٿيندو؟
lines.roman: mubārakūṃ! para riporṭa jo chhā thīndo?
lines.en: Congratulations! But what about the report?

lines.speaker: Asad
lines.native: رپورٽ خميس تائين پوري ٿي ويندي، سائين. وعدو!
lines.roman: riporṭa xamīsa tāīṃ pūrī thī vendī, sāīṃ. vaʿdo!
lines.en: The report will be done by Thursday, sir. I promise!

lines.native: ٺيڪ آهي، موڪل منظور. پر شاديءَ جي مٺائي نه وسارجانءِ!
lines.roman: ṭhīku āhe, mokala manzūru. para shādīa jī miṭhāī na visārijāṃi!
lines.en: All right, leave approved. But don't forget the wedding sweets!

culture:
In Karachi offices you'll hear Sindhi, Urdu and English in the same sentence; in Hyderabad, Sukkur and Larkana — and in Sindh government offices — Sindhi is the everyday office language. Wherever you are, the boss is **سائين** (or **ميڊم**), and talk about him uses the respectful plural: **سائين آفيس ۾ ناهن** 'Sir isn't in'. Calling a superior by first name, or using تون, would be shocking.

Colleagues of your own age become **يار** quickly, and the tea break (**چانهه**) is where friendships and office gossip happen — **ٻڌجي ٿو ته …** 'word is …'. On Fridays offices often break for **جمعي جي نماز** around 1 pm, and in Ramzan working hours are shortened.

Written requests — a leave application, a request to the HR department — are still very formal: **محترم سائين، عرض آهي ته …** and a respectful sign-off. Emails are mostly in English, but WhatsApp messages to the boss are often in Sindhi: keep them short, polite and in the توهان form. Good personal news at work (a wedding, a baby, a promotion) means bringing **مٺائي** for the whole office.

tip.title: At work: سائين، ميڊم، توهان
tip.body:
- To a boss or client always **توهان**, with plural verbs even for one person: علي صاحب ميٽنگ ۾ **آهن**.
- Address: **سائين** (man), **ميڊم** (woman), or name + **صاحب**.
- Answer: **جي سائين** / **حاضر** 'right away'.
- Colleagues your age soon become **تون** and **يار** — but not in meetings.

lessons.title: Meetings and deadlines

tip.title: It was decided: the passive
tip.body:
- Past participle + **وڃڻ**: فيصلو **ڪيو ويو** 'it was decided'.
- Both parts agree with the **thing**: ميٽنگ ملتوي **ڪئي وئي** (f).
- Any tense: ڪيو **وڃي ٿو** (is done) · ڪيو **ويندو** (will be) · ڪيو **ويو آهي** (has been).
- The doer is left out — that's the point.

lessons.title: Asking for leave and more time

tip.title: Writing to your boss
tip.body:
- Open with **محترم سائين** / **محترم ميڊم**.
- Ask with **عرض آهي ته …** + a passive subjunctive: موڪل ڏني **وڃي** 'that leave be given'.
- Close with **مهرباني** and **توهان جو** (man) / **توهان جي** (woman) + your name.
- Even on WhatsApp, keep توهان and سائين.

lessons.title: Getting through a job interview

tip.title: Interview Sindhi
tip.body:
- Expect **توهان** and polite commands: پنهنجي باري ۾ **ٻڌايو**.
- 'About' = **جي باري ۾**; 'experience in' = **۾ تجربو**: مون کي هن ڪم ۾ تجربو آهي.
- Answer in full sentences, starting with **جي** — a bare ها sounds offhand.
